schemas.title: cllcResonant
schemas.description: CLLC Bidirectional Resonant converter excitation. Schema v2 adds asymmetric-tank ratios (a, b), bridge-type selection (full/half) and leakage-integration flags so that Lr1, Lr2 can be either discrete components or absorbed into transformer leakage. The pre-v2 boolean `symmetricDesign` is retained as a derived alias (true iff a==1 && b==1). See Infineon AN-2024-06 §2.3 for the canonical 11-step design procedure and the asymmetric design rationale of Min et al., IEEE TPE 36(6) 2021.

inputVoltage.description: The input voltage (HV side) of the CLLC converter

minSwitchingFrequency.description: The minimum switching frequency for regulation

maxSwitchingFrequency.description: The maximum switching frequency for regulation

qualityFactor.description: Quality factor of the resonant tank, Infineon convention Q = sqrt(Lr/Cr) / Ro. Two other conventions exist in the literature (Steigerwald uses 1/Q, Erickson uses Ro/sqrt(Lr/Cr)); the Infineon convention is documented in the class header.

symmetricDesign.description: DEPRECATED - retained for v1 compatibility. True iff resonantInductorRatio==1 && resonantCapacitorRatio==1. New code should set the ratio fields directly.

bidirectional.description: Whether the converter operates in bidirectional mode (active synchronous rectifier on the secondary side, capable of reverse power flow). When false the secondary still uses SR for efficiency but reverse mode is not exercised.

bridgeType.description: Bridge topology of the primary inverter. Full-bridge gives bridge-voltage factor 1.0 (peak Vpri = Vin); half-bridge gives 0.5 (peak Vpri = Vin/2). Most CLLC > 1 kW use full bridge; sub-1 kW server / V2L designs use half-bridge.

integratedResonantInductor1.description: If true, the primary resonant inductor Lr1 is realised as transformer primary leakage (no discrete inductor). When false, Lr1 is a discrete component placed in series with the primary winding.

integratedResonantInductor2.description: If true, the secondary resonant inductor Lr2 is realised as transformer secondary leakage. When false, Lr2 is a discrete component placed in series with the secondary winding (CLLLC layout).

resonantInductorRatio.description: Asymmetric-tank ratio a = n^2 * Lr2 / Lr1. Symmetric tank: a = 1. Typical asymmetric battery-charger design (Min IEEE TPE 2021): a ~= 0.95.

resonantCapacitorRatio.description: Asymmetric-tank ratio b = Cr2 / (n^2 * Cr1). Symmetric tank: b = 1. Typical asymmetric battery-charger design: b ~= 1.052 so that fr1 = fr2 (a*b ~ 1).

schemas.title: cuk
schemas.description: Cuk converter excitation. Five wiring variants are supported via the boolean flags below: V1 non-isolated (defaults), V2 coupled-inductor zero-ripple (coupledInductor=true), V3 transformer-isolated (isolated=true), V4 synchronous (synchronous=true), V5 bidirectional (bidirectional=true, V4 implied). For V1/V2/V4/V5 the magnetic returned by process_design_requirements is the input inductor L1 (V2: a 2-winding coupled inductor); for V3 it is a 2-winding transformer. The remaining reactive elements (L2, C1, Co, plus Ca/Cb in V3) are emitted via get_extra_components_inputs.

inputVoltage.description: The input voltage of the Cuk

diodeVoltageDrop.description: The voltage drop on the diode (ignored when synchronous=true)

maximumSwitchCurrent.description: The maximum current that can go through the selected switch

currentRippleRatio.description: The maximum input-inductor (L1) current ripple ratio (delta-IL1 / IL1_avg)

synchronous.description: If true, the catch diode D1 is replaced by an actively-driven synchronous switch S2. Reduces conduction loss; mandatory for bidirectional=true.

bidirectional.description: If true, both switches are active and the converter can transfer power in either direction depending on operatingPoint.powerFlow. Implies synchronous=true.

isolated.description: If true, the coupling capacitor is split into Ca/Cb and an isolation transformer is inserted between them. The magnetic returned is the transformer (2 windings, isolation sides PRIMARY and SECONDARY); L1 and L2 become extra components.

coupledInductor.description: If true, L1 and L2 are wound on the same core with coupling coefficient couplingCoefficient (Cuk's zero-ripple trick when k = sqrt(L1/L2)). The magnetic returned is a 2-winding coupled inductor. Mutually exclusive with isolated=true.

turnsRatio.description: Transformer turns ratio Np:Ns for isolated=true (used as Vo/Vin step targeting). Ignored for non-isolated variants.

couplingCoefficient.description: Magnetic coupling coefficient k between L1 and L2 (used only when coupledInductor=true). Zero-ripple condition: k * sqrt(L2/L1) = 1.

couplingCapacitanceSecondary.description: Secondary-side coupling capacitance Cb in farads (used only when isolated=true). If absent, Cb defaults to Ca scaled by turnsRatio^2 to balance V*s on each side.

cukOperatingPoint.description: The description of one Cuk operating point. NOTE: outputVoltages magnitudes are passed positive here; Vo is signed negative internally per Cuk polarity convention. powerFlow is required only when the parent Cuk has bidirectional=true.
cukOperatingPoint.title: cukOperatingPoint

powerFlow.description: Power-flow direction. Forward = source -> load via L1; reverse = load -> source via L2.

schemas.title: dualActiveBridge
schemas.description: Dual Active Bridge (DAB) DC-DC converter excitation. Modulation parameters follow the standard Triple Phase Shift (TPS) convention: D1 = primary-bridge intra-leg shift, D2 = secondary-bridge intra-leg shift, D3 = inter-bridge (outer) shift. See Huang et al., Energies 11(9):2419 (2018) and Maniktala & Rosano, 'Power Supplies A to Z', 3rd ed. (Ch. 2).

inputVoltage.description: The input voltage of the DAB converter

seriesInductance.description: The series inductance for power transfer control. If 0, uses transformer leakage inductance

useLeakageInductance.description: Whether to use transformer leakage inductance as the series inductor

perSecondaryLeakage.description: Optional per-secondary leakage inductance in H, one entry per output. Required for physically meaningful multi-output DAB simulation; if absent, all secondaries share the same series inductance.

dabOperatingPoint.description: One DAB operating point. Modulation is parameterised by three phase-shift variables D1, D2, D3 (Huang et al. 2018 convention): D1 and D2 are intra-bridge (leg-to-leg) shifts that control each bridge's effective duty cycle, and D3 is the outer inter-bridge shift that controls power transfer. SPS uses D3 only (D1=D2=0). EPS uses D3 + one inner shift (D1, with D2=0). DPS uses D3 + one symmetric inner shift (D1=D2). TPS uses all three independently.
dabOperatingPoint.title: dabOperatingPoint

modulationType.description: DAB modulation scheme. SPS (only D3), EPS (D1>0, D2=0), DPS (D1=D2>0), TPS (independent). Ref: Huang et al., Energies 11(9):2419 (2018).

schemas.title: fourSwitchBuckBoost
schemas.description: 4-Switch Buck-Boost (also called non-inverting buck-boost, H-bridge buck-boost, FSBB) excitation. Single inductor with two half-bridges (Q1/Q2 buck leg, Q3/Q4 boost leg). The controller selects one of three operating regions per Vin value: BUCK (Vo/Vin < 1-hysteresis: Q3 always-on, Q1/Q2 PWM), BOOST (Vo/Vin > 1+hysteresis: Q1 always-on, Q3/Q4 PWM), or BUCK_BOOST (transition band: all four switches modulate). The magnetic returned by process_design_requirements is the single inductor sized for the worst-case region across the Vin sweep (max(L_buck@VinMax, L_boost@VinMin)). Cin and Co are emitted via get_extra_components_inputs. References: TI SLVA535B, TI LM5175/LM5176, ADI LT8390, Restrepo IEEE 8986423.

maximumSwitchCurrent.description: The maximum current that can go through any of the four switches

currentRippleRatio.description: The maximum inductor current ripple ratio (delta-IL / IL_avg)

outputVoltageRippleRatio.description: The output voltage ripple ratio (delta-Vo / Vo)

controlMode.description: Controller duty-assignment strategy in the buck-boost region (peakCurrent: TI LM5176, peakBuckPeakBoost: ADI LT8390, averageCurrent: USB-PD, voltageMode: legacy)

transitionMode.description: Buck-boost-region modulation: 'simultaneous' (Mode 1, Q1+Q3 ON together) or 'splitPwm' (Mode 2, sequential split-PWM, LM5176/LT8390 default)

bidirectional.description: If true, controller allows reverse power flow (V2G / battery / 12V<->48V mild-hybrid)

phaseCount.description: Number of interleaved phases (default 1; >1 for automotive 12V<->48V)

transitionHysteresisRatio.description: Width of the buck-boost band as |1 - Vo/Vin| (default 0.15 per LM5176)

schemas.title: powerFactorCorrection
schemas.description: The description of a Power Factor Correction (PFC) stage. PFC converters shape the input current to follow the input voltage waveform, achieving near-unity power factor. The inductor operates with a triangular current ripple superimposed on a half-sinusoidal envelope. This topology covers both continuous (CCM) and discontinuous (DCM) conduction modes across the standard single-phase and three-phase variants (boost, bridgeless, totem-pole, interleaved boost, Vienna, etc.).

inputVoltage.description: The AC input voltage (RMS) with tolerance range (e.g., 85-265V universal input)

outputVoltage.description: The DC output voltage (typically 385-400V for universal input)

lineFrequency.description: The AC line frequency (50 or 60 Hz)

switchingFrequency.description: The switching frequency of the PFC stage

currentRippleRatio.description: The peak-to-peak current ripple as a ratio of the average current (typically 0.2-0.4 for CCM)

efficiency.description: The target efficiency of the PFC stage

mode.description: The conduction mode of the PFC

topologyVariant.description: The PFC topology variant. 'boost' is the classical single-phase boost PFC (full-bridge rectifier + boost stage), the default. 'bridgeless' / 'semiBridgeless' / 'totemPole' eliminate the input rectifier bridge for higher efficiency. 'interleavedBoost' uses N>=2 parallel boost cells phase-shifted for ripple cancellation. 'vienna' is the 3-phase 3-level rectifier used in telecom and EV chargers. 'buck' / 'buckBoost' / 'sepic' / 'cuk' are step-down or buck-boost variants used in low-power LED drivers and isolated PFC stages.

numberOfPhases.description: Number of parallel phases / interleaved cells. 1 for boost/bridgeless/totemPole/buck variants; 2 or 3 for interleavedBoost; 3 for vienna.

wideBandgapSwitch.description: Whether the active switches are wide-bandgap (GaN/SiC) devices. Required true for totem-pole CCM PFC (Si MOSFET body-diode reverse recovery makes CCM totem-pole infeasible).

bulkCapacitance.description: The DC bus bulk capacitance in farads. Used by the operating-point synthesis to compute the twice-line-frequency bus-voltage ripple: ΔVbus ≈ Pout / (2·π·f_line·Cbus·Vbus). Sized in practice from hold-up-time requirements (~1–4 µF/W of output power for 230 Vrms input, 400 V bus, 20 ms hold-up).

maximumSwitchCurrent.description: The maximum current rating of the switch (optional constraint)

pfcModes.title: pfcModes

schemas.title: sepic
schemas.description: SEPIC (Single-Ended Primary-Inductor Converter) excitation. Non-inverting fourth-order DC-DC converter with capacitive energy transfer through the coupling capacitor Cs between L1 and L2. Two wiring variants are supported via the boolean flags below: V1 uncoupled (defaults; L1 and L2 are independent inductors) and V2 coupled-inductor (coupledInductor=true; L1 and L2 share one core, ripple-steering per TI SLYT411). Optional synchronousRectifier replaces the catch diode with a low-side MOSFET. The magnetic returned by process_design_requirements is the input inductor L1 (or, when coupledInductor=true, a 2-winding coupled inductor). The remaining reactive elements (L2, Cs, Co) are emitted via get_extra_components_inputs.

inputVoltage.description: The input voltage of the SEPIC

diodeVoltageDrop.description: The voltage drop on the rectifier diode (ignored when synchronousRectifier=true)

maximumSwitchCurrent.description: The maximum current that can go through the selected switch

currentRippleRatio.description: The maximum input-inductor (L1) current ripple ratio (delta-IL1 / IL1_avg)

synchronousRectifier.description: If true, the catch diode is replaced by an actively-driven low-side synchronous MOSFET. Reduces conduction loss; common at low Vout.

coupledInductor.description: If true, L1 and L2 are wound on the same core (1:1 coupled) with coupling coefficient couplingCoefficient. Ripple-steering per TI SLYT411 reduces input-current ripple. The magnetic returned is a 2-winding coupled inductor.

couplingCoefficient.description: Magnetic coupling coefficient k between L1 and L2 (used only when coupledInductor=true). Typical values 0.95-0.999.

sepicOperatingPoint.description: The description of one SEPIC operating point. SEPIC outputs are non-inverting (Vo positive).
sepicOperatingPoint.title: sepicOperatingPoint

schemas.title: seriesResonant
schemas.description: The description of a Series Resonant Converter (SRC) excitation. Two-element series Lr+Cr tank with no Lm branch. Gain M <= 1 (step-down only). Steigerwald 1988; Kazimierczuk Ch. 4. See src/converter_models/SRC_PLAN.md for the full design rationale.

inputVoltage.description: The input voltage of the SRC converter

minSwitchingFrequency.description: The minimum switching frequency for regulation

maxSwitchingFrequency.description: The maximum switching frequency for regulation

resonantFrequency.description: The resonant frequency fr = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(Lr*Cr)) of the tank (optional, will be calculated if not provided)

schemas.title: weinberg
schemas.description: Weinberg DC-DC converter (current-fed push-pull-derivative, isolated, boost-capable). Spacecraft-heritage topology featuring a 1:1 input coupled inductor L1 with energy-recovery diode D3 to Vin, plus a center-tapped main transformer with center-tapped full-wave secondary rectifier. Intrinsically supports switch overlap above D=0.5 (boost regime) without needing a freewheel switch. Variants supported: V1 classic (push-pull primary, 2 switches) and V2 bridge (H-bridge primary, 4 switches) via the `variant` flag; optional synchronousRectifier replaces secondary diodes with active SR MOSFETs. The magnetic returned by process_design_requirements is the main 2-winding transformer (n = Np_total/Ns_total); the input coupled inductor L1 and output capacitor Co are emitted via get_extra_components_inputs.

schemas.title: zeta
schemas.description: Zeta excitation. Non-inverting fourth-order DC-DC converter — the dual of SEPIC: same gain M = D/(1-D), but the LC filter is on the OUTPUT side (so output-voltage ripple is small and there is no right-half-plane zero in CCM). The switch is HIGH-SIDE (PFET by default in the SPICE model). Two wiring variants are supported via the boolean flags below: V1 uncoupled (defaults; L1 magnetizing and L2 output filter are independent inductors) and V2 coupled-inductor (coupledInductor=true; L1 and L2 share one core, ripple-steering per TI SLYT411 — same condition as coupled-SEPIC because both inductors see identical voltages during both subintervals). Optional synchronousRectifier replaces the catch diode with a low-side MOSFET. The magnetic returned by process_design_requirements is L1 (or, when coupledInductor=true, a 2-winding coupled inductor). The remaining reactive elements (L2, Cc, Co) are emitted via get_extra_components_inputs.

coreElectricalReference.description: How the core is referenced electrically in the assembled component. A ferrite or powder core has no terminal of its own: it sits at whatever potential the surrounding conductors impose on it, unless it is deliberately bonded, through a mounting clip, a copper strap or flux band, or conductive tape, to a circuit reference or to one end of a winding. The choice decides how the winding-to-core capacitances appear at the terminals (a charge-balanced floating node gives C0/12 of a winding's distributed capacitance for a linear potential ramp; a core tied to either end of that winding gives C0/3; the live end innermost against a bonded core approaches C0) and whether the primary-to-core-to-secondary common-mode path is closed through the core or diverted to the reference. Absent means floating: a core with no clip, strap or tape, which is also the assumption every model made before this field existed.

material.description: The material(s) the core is made of. A single material (by record or by name) for the overwhelming majority of cores. A LIST when the assembly genuinely comprises pieces of different grades that the analytical models must treat separately — e.g. a shielded drum whose closing ring is a different ferrite from the drum (ABT #576). Order is significant: the FIRST entry is the primary piece (the drum / the wound piece), subsequent entries are the closing pieces in the order the magnetic circuit crosses them. A one-element list means the same thing as the bare form. For the molded family the entries are the REGIONS of one pressed body rather than separate pieces, in the order the flux crosses them from the post upward: a two-entry list is [post, rest] (the inner and outer powders of a body pressed in two steps), a three-entry list is [post, cover, base] (a body pressed in three steps: the base plate, the post, and the cover moulded over the coil). The reserved name "air" may stand in the post position only, and means the coil sits on a plastic bobbin with no magnetic post inside it (ABT #1002).

oneOf.description: Magnetic component (inductor, transformer, choke) — defined by MAS.
Capacitor — defined by CAS.
Semiconductor (MOSFET, diode, IGBT, BJT) — defined by SAS.
Resistor — defined by RAS.
Varistor (MOV / multilayer) — defined by RAS alongside resistor; voltage-dependent protection element.

Thermistor (NTC / PTC) — defined by RAS alongside resistor and varistor; temperature-dependent resistor for inrush limiting and temperature sensing/compensation. Resettable polymer PTC fuses (PPTC) are protection parts, out of scope.

Control IC (PWM / multiphase / LLC / PFC / phase-shift / sync-rectifier / digital / gate-driver / shunt-regulator / voltage-reference / current-sense / isolated amplifier / hot-swap / eFuse) — defined by CTAS. Extracted from the former inline PEAS branch into the CTAS sibling repo; CTAS owns the controller-family enums while reusing the PEAS shared primitives.

Connector — defined by CONAS. Covers the full range of board-boundary conductors: screw terminals (terminalBlock), solder pads, pin headers, edge-card, wire-to-board, RF, power, etc. A minimal Tier-1-only CONAS doc (connector: {}) with inputs.designRequirements (connectorFamily + electrical ratings) is valid for pre-librarian abstract-boundary seeds; manufacturerInfo is populated after librarian binding.

Analog IC (op amp, comparator, instrumentation/difference amp, PGA, buffer/line driver, sample-and-hold, analog switch, multiplexer, ADC, DAC) — generic analog/linear parts, defined by AAS. Distinct from CTAS (power-control ICs) and SAS (discrete power semiconductors).

Time-base component (crystal / XO / TCXO / VCXO / OCXO / MEMS / silicon-RC / programmable oscillator, 555-class timer, SR latch) — defined by TBAS. The families carry ideal `behavioral` blocks (periodic source / one-shot / latch), so an anonymous PWM ramp in a CIAS control brick and an orderable oscillator are the same type. Distinct from CTAS (power-control ICs) and AAS (analog signal path).

Potentiometer / rheostat / trimmer — defined by RAS alongside resistor, varistor and thermistor. A THREE-terminal adjustable divider, not a resistor with an extra field: the electrical model is two resistances summing to `totalResistance`, split at a design-time wiper position. It is its own discriminator because a potentiometer SATISFIES `resistor.electrical`'s required set, so filing one as a fixed resistor would validate silently rather than fail.

Connector accessory — defined by CONAS. Backshells, bare crimp and solder contacts, hoods, caps, IC and memory sockets, EMI gaskets, TPA retainers, cages, marker cards, tooling. Separate from `connector` because that family describes a MATED interface and requires `electrical`, `mechanical` and `familyDetails`: a backshell has no mating face, no contact count and no electrical rating, so three of those four blocks are structurally unavailable rather than merely unsourced.

Relay — electromechanical, reed, solid-state, hybrid or mercury-wetted — defined by EMAS. A contact set operated by a separate input, so `electrical.input` is a pinned union rather than a coil block: a solid-state relay's opto-isolated input cannot honestly be described as a coil.

Switch — push-button, tactile, toggle, snap-action, slide, rocker, DIP/SIP, keylock and rotary, with circuit breakers as a pinned variant — defined by EMAS. Shares EMAS's load-side contact model with `relay`; the difference is what moves the contacts, an actuator rather than an input signal.

Behavioral (mathematical model) component — an element whose constitutive relation is expressed as an analytic formula, a parametric Chan saturable-core model, or a coupled-inductor inductance matrix. Simulator-agnostic: CiasCircuitConverter generates the correct syntax for each target (ngspice B-element with ddt(), LTspice FLux=/Q= or Hc/Bs/…, L/K inductor-coupling cards, Verilog-A contribution statement).
Distributed transmission line (lossy or lossless; SPICE O / .model LTRA) — a 2-port element defined by per-unit-length RLGC and a length. A PEAS-native primitive with no external family schema.

allOf.$comment: Pin inputs.designRequirements shape to the populated discriminator branch.

behavioralDesignRequirements.title: behavioralDesignRequirements
behavioralDesignRequirements.description: Design-requirements seed for the PEAS-native primitives (behavioral, transmissionLine). They have no family repo, so the seed carries only an optional label; all electrical definition lives in the component branch itself.

behavioral.title: Behavioral
behavioral.description: An element whose constitutive relation is given analytically. Most natures are two-terminal (expression-based flux linkage Ψ(i) or charge Q(v,i), the parametric Chan saturable-core model); 'controlled'/'source'/'switch'/'frequencyResponse' name their own pins explicitly, and 'coupledInductors' is the one 2N-terminal nature (N windings, matrix-defined). Variables in expressions are fixed by convention: i = port current [A], v = branch voltage [V], temp = temperature [°C], time = simulation time [s]; standard math functions (exp, abs, sqrt, sin, cos, atan, log) are valid. time maps to LTspice/ngspice `time` and Verilog-A $abstime; it enables soft-start ramps and bespoke stimuli without dedicated natures.

oneOf.description: Expression-based constitutive relation. nature='flux' defines Ψ(i)=expression [V·s]; nature='charge' defines Q(v,i)=expression [C]. CiasCircuitConverter emits: LTspice→FLux=/Q= with x=i or x=v; ngspice→B-element with V=ddt(expr(I(Vsense))) or I=ddt(expr(V(a,b))); Verilog-A→Phi(br)<+expr or Q(br)<+expr.

nature.description: Physical quantity being defined: 'flux' for flux-linkage Ψ(i) [V·s], 'charge' for charge Q(v,i) [C].

expression.description: Analytic expression using i (this component's own port current [A]), v (its branch voltage [V]), i(<designator>) (the branch current of a sibling 'source' component in the same brick — e.g. a shared port-current sense), and standard math functions. E.g. '1e-9*i*(12.897*exp(-0.04309*abs(i))+119.58*exp(-0.8347*abs(i)))'.

oneOf.description: Chan saturable core model (LTspice Hc/Bs/Br/A/Lm/Lg/N parameters). NOTE: despite widespread use of the name, LTspice implements the Chan 1991 model (IEEE Trans. CAD), not the Jiles-Atherton model — parameters are not inter-convertible without B-H curve fitting. CiasCircuitConverter emits: LTspice→L Hc=… Bs=… Br=… A=… Lm=… Lg=… N=…; ngspice→Chan/JA Verilog-A subcircuit (ngspice ≥36 via OSDI) or approximate saturation B-element; Verilog-A→Chan analog module.

coercive_force.description: Hc [A/m] — coercive field strength. The B-H material parameters (Hc/Bs/Br) may be temperature-dependent (LTspice tbl(temp,...)).

saturation_flux_density.description: Bs [T] — flux density at saturation. May be temperature-dependent.

remanence_flux_density.description: Br [T] — residual flux density after deenergisation. May be temperature-dependent.

magnetic_path_length.description: Lm [m] — mean magnetic path length of the core (geometry, NOT an inductance). LTspice Chan calls this Lm.

effective_area.description: A [m^2] — effective core cross-sectional area (geometry, NOT a domain density). LTspice Chan calls this A.

oneOf.description: Controlled / dependent source: an ideal behavioral source whose value is a function of THIS component's own terminal voltages and currents, plus (by name) the branch current of a sibling 'source' component in the same brick — it never reaches into arbitrary external nets. Subsumes VCVS/VCCS/CCVS/CCCS and nonlinear behavioral relations (op-amp gain, current mirror, gyrator, varistor/TVS clamp i(v)). The expression references own pins as v(p,q) (voltage between own pins) and i(p,q) (current into pin p via the p->q branch) plus standard math and pwl(x, x1,y1, ...). Finite input/output impedance is modeled with sibling R/C components, not here. CiasCircuitConverter emits a B-source between the 'across' pins (V= or I=), substituting v()/i() with the wired nodes and synthesising a 0 V sense for each i(); pwl maps to LTspice table().

quantity.description: 'voltage' forces V(across[0],across[1]) = expression; 'current' injects I from across[0] to across[1] = expression.

across.description: The two OWN pin names the source is applied between.

expression.description: Function of this component's own terminals, plus named sibling current senses: v(p,q), i(p,q), i(<designator>) (the branch current of a sibling 'source' component in the same brick — e.g. a shared port-current sense), time (simulation time [s]; LTspice/ngspice `time`, Verilog-A $abstime), standard math, pwl(x, x1,y1, x2,y2, ...). E.g. VCVS 'gain*v(inp,inn)', VCCS 'gm*v(inp,inn)', CCVS 'r*i(inp,inn)', CCCS 'beta*i(inp,inn)', clamp 'pwl(v(a,b), v1,i1, ...)'.

oneOf.description: Fixed internal source that is part of a component macromodel (NOT external stimulus — that enters via ports/TAS). nature='source' forces a constant voltage across, or current through, its 'across' pins. A voltage source of value 0 is an ideal ammeter (current sense): its branch current is referenceable from a sibling behavioral expression as i(<designator>). CiasCircuitConverter emits V<name> a b <value> (voltage) or I<name> a b <value> (current).

quantity.description: 'voltage' forces V(across[0],across[1]) = value; 'current' injects I from across[0] to across[1] = value.

across.description: The two OWN pin names the source is applied between.

value.description: Constant value [V] or [A]. Use 0 for a pure current sense (ideal ammeter).

oneOf.description: Voltage-controlled hysteretic switch (SPICE S / .model SW). Conducts 'ron' once V(control) rises through vOn and 'roff' once it falls through vOff; the vOn/vOff gap is the hysteresis that makes ESD snapback protection work. Four own pins: the switched path 'across' and the controlling pair 'control'. CiasCircuitConverter emits S<name> across+ across- control+ control- <model> + .model <model> SW(Ron= Roff= Von= Voff=).

across.description: The two OWN pins of the switched path.

control.description: The two OWN pins whose voltage controls the switch.

vOn.description: Control voltage [V] at/above which the switch turns on.

vOff.description: Control voltage [V] at/below which the switch turns off.

oneOf.description: Frequency-domain controlled source (SPICE E/G FREQ table). Output = H(f)*control, where H(f) is a tabulated complex transfer function — one entry of a Touchstone S-matrix (e.g. a WE-CLFS filter's S_ij). CiasCircuitConverter emits E<name> across+ across- FREQ {V(control+,control-)}= MAG (f mag phase)(...), converting the stored linear magnitude and radian phase to the target's convention.

quantity.description: 'voltage' forces V(across[0],across[1]) = H(f)*V(control); 'current' injects that current from across[0] to across[1].

control.description: The two OWN pins whose voltage is the controlling input V(control[0],control[1]).

points.description: Tabulated transfer function H(f), one entry per frequency, ascending.

oneOf.description: Coupled-inductor bundle: N magnetically coupled windings defined by the full N×N inductance matrix (e.g. a connector pin-field partial-inductance model, a busbar loop, a multi-phase coupled choke). Element [i][j] is the mutual inductance M_ij [H]; the diagonal L_ii is winding i's self (partial) inductance. The matrix is expected symmetric positive-definite: consumers MUST reject (never clamp) asymmetry beyond numeric tolerance, a non-positive diagonal, or |k_ij| = |M_ij|/sqrt(L_ii*L_jj) > 1. Pin convention: winding i (1-based, in matrix row order) exposes the pin pair 'winding<i>_start' / 'winding<i>_end' — the N-winding generalization of the magnetic branch's primary_start/primary_end naming; a CIAS brick binds these pin names to nets exactly like any other component pins. Sign convention: M_ij > 0 means currents entering both _start pins produce adding flux (the dot sits at every _start). CiasCircuitConverter emits one inductor per winding, L<name>_<i> between the winding's nodes with value L_ii, plus K<name>_<i>_<j> L<name>_<i> L<name>_<j> k_ij for every i<j with M_ij != 0 (k_ij = M_ij/sqrt(L_ii*L_jj)); a seriesResistance entry lowers to a series R<name>_<i> through an internal node.

inductanceMatrix.description: N×N inductance matrix [H], row-major: element [i][j] is the mutual M_ij between windings i and j; the diagonal [i][i] is the self inductance L_ii (> 0). Must be square and symmetric (M_ij = M_ji) and is expected positive-definite; consumers validate and throw on violation.

seriesResistance.description: Optional per-winding series resistance [Ω], one entry per winding in matrix row order (length must equal N). Lowered as a resistor in series with winding i's inductor.

transmissionLine.title: transmissionLine
transmissionLine.description: Distributed 2-port transmission line (SPICE O / .model LTRA). Four pins: in+, in-, out+, out-. 'kind' selects the loss model; 'lossy' carries per-unit-length R/L/C(/G) and a length. CiasCircuitConverter emits O<name> in+ in- out+ out- <model> + .model <model> LTRA(len=… R=… L=… C=… G=…).

kind.description: Loss model: 'lossy' (RLGC per unit length) or 'lossless' (LC only).

resistance.description: R [Ω/m] — series resistance per unit length.

inductance.description: L [H/m] — series inductance per unit length.

capacitance.description: C [F/m] — shunt capacitance per unit length.

conductance.description: G [S/m] — shunt conductance per unit length (default 0).

behavioralTemperatureValue.title: behavioralTemperatureValue
behavioralTemperatureValue.description: A scalar in a behavioral model that may vary with temperature. Either a plain number (temperature-independent) or a set of (temperature, value) breakpoints that reproduce the source LTspice tbl(temp, T1,v1, T2,v2, ...) table; consumers interpolate, and a non-interpolating consumer resolves at referenceTemperature.

referenceTemperature.description: Temperature in degrees Celsius at which a non-interpolating consumer should resolve this quantity (e.g. 25).

perTemperature.description: Breakpoints of the value versus temperature, reproducing the source tbl(temp, ...) table.

temperature.description: Temperature in degrees Celsius.

manufacturer.description: Manufacturer of the substitute. Omitted on a 'successor' entry it means the same manufacturer as this part, since a manufacturer supersedes its own part; write it anyway, and it MUST be written when it differs.

type.description: Kind of substitution. 'successor' is directional and asserts that THIS part is superseded by the named one - one hop, as the manufacturer states it, never inferred from an obsolete status or from a part-number pattern; a successor that is itself superseded names its own successor on its own record. The other values are symmetric: either part may be bought in place of the other.

datasheetInfoThermal.title: datasheetInfoThermal
datasheetInfoThermal.description: Shared thermal section for datasheetInfo: operating temperature as dimensionWithTolerance (minimum = min operating, maximum = max operating). Open base — families extend by allOf and close the composed object with additionalProperties:false on the extension branch.

operatingTemperature.description: Operating temperature range in degrees Celsius.

datasheetInfoMechanical.title: datasheetInfoMechanical
datasheetInfoMechanical.description: Shared mechanical section for datasheetInfo: named dimensions as dimensionWithTolerance, assembly type, weight, and shape. Open base — families extend by allOf + unevaluatedProperties:false.

diameter.description: Body diameter in metres (for cylindrical parts).

datasheetInfoPartBase.title: datasheetInfoPartBase
datasheetInfoPartBase.description: Universal part-identification fields shared by every component family. Open base — families extend by allOf + unevaluatedProperties:false, adding family-specific fields (technology, dielectricCode, subType, etc.).

series.description: Product series or product-line name (null where the part has no distinct series).

description.description: Free-text part description as on the datasheet.

datasheetInfoThermalSemiconductor.title: datasheetInfoThermalSemiconductor
datasheetInfoThermalSemiconductor.description: Semiconductor-specific thermal section for datasheetInfo: junction thermal resistances, temperature limits, and an optional Foster RC-ladder model.

thermalResistanceJunctionCase.description: Junction-to-case thermal resistance R_th(j-c), in K/W.

thermalResistanceJunctionAmbient.description: Junction-to-ambient thermal resistance R_th(j-a), in K/W.

thermalResistanceCaseSink.description: Case-to-heatsink thermal resistance R_th(c-s), in K/W.

junctionTemperatureMax.description: Absolute maximum junction temperature T_j(max), in °C.

fosterNetwork.description: Foster RC ladder thermal model. Each element is {resistance: K/W, timeConstant: seconds} in order from junction outward.

resistance.description: Thermal resistance of this cell, in K/W.

timeConstant.description: Thermal time constant of this cell, in seconds.

datasheetInfoLifetime.title: datasheetInfoLifetime
datasheetInfoLifetime.description: Reliability and lifetime parameters for components with wear-out mechanisms. Model: L = L0 × (V0/V)^aexp × exp(bexp × (1/T - 1/T0)). All lifetime values in hours unless stated. Open base — families extend by allOf and close the composed object on the extension branch. Numeric fields accept null (datasheets routinely omit individual model parameters).

lifetimeEndurance.description: Rated endurance life in hours at rated conditions (voltage, temperature).

maxLifetime.description: Maximum expected service lifetime in years.

aexp.description: Voltage stress exponent for the lifetime model (exponent on V0/V ratio).

bexp.description: Temperature stress coefficient for the lifetime model (Arrhenius exponent).

deltaT0.description: Reference temperature differential ΔT0 in °C for the lifetime model.

kfactor.description: K factor (voltage derating exponent or scaling constant) for the lifetime model.

vxfactor.description: Vx factor for extended voltage lifetime model.

usefulLife.description: Useful life in hours (IEC 62863 / IEC 61709 definition: time to specified end-of-life criteria).

manufacturerInfo.title: manufacturerInfo
manufacturerInfo.description: Shared manufacturer-info fields. Each component family builds its OWN closed manufacturerInfo by $ref-ing these field definitions (by JSON pointer) and adding its datasheetInfo; families do NOT allOf-extend this (incompatible with additionalProperties:false).

name.description: Manufacturer name

description.description: Description of the part per its manufacturer

family.description: Manufacturer product family / product-line name (e.g. 'CoolMOS C7', 'WE-MAPI').

series.description: Manufacturer product series within the family.

spiceModel.description: SPICE simulation model for this component

provenance.description: Where this component's data came from. Optional here so that any PEAS-based record carrying manufacturerInfo -- including ones whose own schema has no datasheet-info section, such as a bobbin -- can cite the source of each value rather than only a datasheet URL.

resultOrigin.description: Origin of the value of an output result. Mirror of MAS schemas/outputs.json#/$defs/resultOrigin.
resultOrigin.title: resultOrigin

twoDimensionalMatrix.description: Generic two-dimensional numeric matrix (array of arrays of numbers). Mirror of MAS schemas/utils.json#/$defs/twoDimensionalMatrix.
twoDimensionalMatrix.title: twoDimensionalMatrix

topology.description: Power-electronics converter topology, used by every family's designRequirements to tag which converter a component is designed for (e.g. a capacitor's stress/lifetime model depends on it). PEAS HOSTS this shared vocabulary because all families reference it and PEAS is the only layer beneath them all; MAS OWNS its content (MAS implements the converter topologies under inputs/topologies/ and is the IEC standard candidate). This enum must mirror MAS's implemented topology set exactly — add a value here only when MAS adds the corresponding topology.
topology.title: topology

market.description: Target market segment for the component. Common to MAS / CAS / RAS / SAS.
market.title: market

maximumDimensions.description: Maximum allowed bounding-box dimensions for the component, in metres.
maximumDimensions.title: maximumDimensions

componentPort.title: componentPort
componentPort.description: Identifier of one electrical port / terminal / winding of a component. Free-form non-empty string so each family can use its own vocabulary (e.g. 'gate'/'drain'/'source' for MOSFETs, 'anode'/'cathode' for diodes, 'primary'/'secondary1' for transformer windings, 'a'/'b' for capacitors and resistors).

designRequirementsBase.description: Family-agnostic outer shell of designRequirements. Each family schema does allOf [designRequirementsBase, family-specific]; the family layer adds its required primary specs (capacitance/resistance/inductance/voltage), narrows 'role' and 'allowedTechnologies' to per-family enums, and adds family-specific optional fields (lifetime, ESR, TCR, gate-charge, etc.).
designRequirementsBase.title: designRequirementsBase

name.description: A label that identifies these Design Requirements

role.description: The role this component plays in the converter. The family schema overrides this with a per-family enum; this base layer leaves it as a string for extensibility.

allowedTechnologies.description: Subset of technologies acceptable for this design. Each family schema overrides 'items' with a per-family enum.

operatingTemperature.description: Required values for the temperature that the component can reach under operation, in Celsius

terminalType.description: Type(s) of terminal that must be used. An array so multi-terminal/multi-winding parts (e.g. magnetics) can require a type per terminal; single-terminal families may supply a one-element array.

maximumWeight.description: Maximum weight for the designed component, in Kg

application.description: Broad application category. Family schemas override this property with a per-family enum ($ref to magneticApplication / capacitorApplication / resistorApplication / semiconductorApplication).

subApplication.description: Narrower sub-application within the chosen application. Family schemas override this property with a per-family enum.

magneticApplication.description: Magnetic component application. Mirror of MAS schemas/utils.json#/$defs/application — kept in PEAS so MAS stays the IEC source of truth without other families taking a runtime dependency on MAS. Update here whenever MAS updates.
magneticApplication.title: magneticApplication

magneticSubApplication.description: Magnetic component sub-application. Mirror of MAS schemas/utils.json#/$defs/subApplication.
magneticSubApplication.title: magneticSubApplication

capacitorApplication.description: Capacitor application category. Aligned with the IEC 60384 sectional-specification structure: power (DC link, line filter, hold-up), signal (decoupling, coupling, timing), safetyEmcSuppression (IEC 60384-14 X/Y classes), motorRunStart (AC across-the-line, IEC 60252).
capacitorApplication.title: capacitorApplication

capacitorSubApplication.description: Capacitor sub-application. The X1/X2/X3/Y1/Y2/Y4 values are the IEC 60384-14 safety/EMC classes (across-the-line vs. line-to-ground, with surge-voltage tiers). Other values further specialize 'power' and 'signal'.
capacitorSubApplication.title: capacitorSubApplication

resistorApplication.description: Resistor application category. Aligned with IEC 60115 sectional specifications and common datasheet usage groupings: power (high dissipation), precision (low TCR / low drift, instrumentation, audio), currentSense (low-ohm shunts, Kelvin connection), pulseHandling (surge/inrush), general (catch-all for standard fixed resistors).
resistorApplication.title: resistorApplication

semiconductorApplication.description: Semiconductor application category. Aligned with JEDEC device classifications and common power-electronics roles: powerSwitching (MOSFET/IGBT used for switching), powerRectification (diodes used as rectifiers, freewheeling, synchronous), protection (TVS/ESD per IEC 61000-4-2/-4-5), signalProcessing (small-signal switching/amplification), referenceClamp (Zener references and clamps).
semiconductorApplication.title: semiconductorApplication

currencyAmount.description: Monetary value with explicit ISO 4217 currency code. Mirrors MAS/utils.json#/$defs/cost. Lifted to PEAS so CAS/RAS/SAS/COAS may reference a single canonical definition.
currencyAmount.title: currencyAmount

currency.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code (EUR, USD, CNY, JPY, ...).

isolationClass.description: Insulation class per IEC 60664-1 / IEC 62368-1. Mirror of MAS/utils.json#/$defs/insulationType.
isolationClass.title: isolationClass

pollutionDegree.description: IEC 60664-1 pollution degree. String form PD1..PD4 (the original MAS vocabulary, kept family-wide so pre-existing MAS documents remain valid).
pollutionDegree.title: pollutionDegree

mountingStyle.description: Mechanical mounting style at the product (not component) level. Used by COAS for converter form-factor.
mountingStyle.title: mountingStyle

environmentalQualification.description: Environmental qualification envelope a product must satisfy. Common to converter (COAS) and component (MAS/CAS/RAS/SAS) levels.
environmentalQualification.title: environmentalQualification

ambientTemperature.description: Operating ambient temperature range, in degrees Celsius.

storageTemperature.description: Non-operating storage temperature range, in degrees Celsius.

altitudeMax.description: Maximum operating altitude in metres above sea level.

ipRating.description: IEC 60529 ingress-protection code (IP00..IP69 with X wildcards allowed).

complianceTarget.description: A single compliance target the product must meet. Open vocabulary for `standard` (e.g. IEC 62368-1, CISPR 32, FCC Part 15, IEC 61000-4-5, IEC 61000-3-2). `class` / `level` are standard-specific enumeration tags (e.g. CISPR Class B, surge Level 4).
complianceTarget.title: complianceTarget

qualifiedReliability.description: A reliability grade the part is QUALIFIED to under a named specification — part IDENTITY, like a safety class or a dielectric code, not a predicted or calculated figure. MIL-PRF-39003 and MIL-PRF-39006 print ONE ratings row covering all of their failure-rate levels, so parts that differ only in this grade are otherwise identical: without this def, 4,878 of 6,373 MIL capacitor rows are byte-identical apart from a dash number and nothing in the record says which level each is. It lives in PEAS rather than in CAS because it is not capacitor-specific — 2,674 magnetics carry a QPL qualification too, and PEAS already owns the requirement-side siblings `reliabilityStandard`, `complianceTarget` and `environmentalQualification` with nothing on the part side. Distinct from `reliabilityStandard`, which names a PREDICTION method (MIL-HDBK-217F, FIDES) applied by an analyst; this records what the qualifying body certified.
qualifiedReliability.title: qualifiedReliability

specification.description: The qualifying specification, e.g. 'MIL-PRF-39003', 'MIL-PRF-39006', 'MIL-PRF-39014', or a QPL designation. Open vocabulary: new specifications appear faster than an enum can be revised, and an unknown string is more useful than a rejected record.

grade.description: The failure-rate level as the specification itself letters it — M, P, R, S for the exponential levels and G, B, C, D for the Weibull ones under MIL-PRF-39003. Kept as the printed token rather than decoded, because the same letter means different rates under different specifications.

failureRate.description: Failure rate in SI base units: failures per SECOND (1/s). Vendors print this as %/1000 h or as FIT, so convert on the way in — 1.0 %/1000 h is 2.7778e-9 1/s, and 1 FIT (one failure per 1e9 hours) is 2.7778e-13 1/s. SI is kept here rather than admitting a third documented unit exception; consumers convert back to FIT for display.

distribution.description: Which failure model the rate is stated under. Load-bearing, not decorative: under MIL-PRF-39003 grades M and G are BOTH 1.0 %/1000 h and are distinguished only by this — M is exponential, G is Weibull — so a record carrying the rate without the distribution has lost the difference between two real, separately orderable parts.

confidenceLevel.description: Confidence level the rate is qualified at, as a FRACTION (0.9, not 90) — the house convention for ratios, as with `dissipationFactor`.

provenance.title: provenance
provenance.description: Data-provenance trail for this record's data. A list, because different fields may come from different sources (e.g. core specs from the manufacturer datasheet, current rating from a distributor, a missing field back-filled by librarian enrichment). Most records that carry this are PARTS, where the trail describes their datasheetInfo — but the definition is deliberately record-neutral: CIAS $refs it for a whole circuit brick, which has no datasheetInfo at all, and a DERIVED brick's trail describes how the brick itself was generated.

source.description: Kind of source this data came from. 'derived' marks values COMPUTED from other fields of the same record (never measured, never read from a document) — a derived entry must say how in `derivation`, so a consumer can distinguish vendor fact from arithmetic.

verification.description: What was actually DONE to establish this entry, as a closed vocabulary. `source` says WHERE the data is claimed to come from; `verification` says HOW FAR anyone got in confirming that claim. The two are independent: a manufacturerDatasheet entry may be anything from notAttempted to valuesReadFromSource. ABSENT means UNSTATED — never a claim of verification — which is what makes this key additive for the 1.7M entries written before it existed. Values, weakest to strongest: 'notAttempted' nobody tried to confirm the claim; 'sourceUnreachable' a fetch was attempted and the source could not be reached (dead URL, gated host, network failure) — evidence about the CITATION, never about the part; 'documentUnreadable' the source was retrieved but yields no usable content (scanned image, no text layer, textless CAD drawing); 'citationOnly' the cited document was retrieved and is a real document, but nothing in it was matched to this record; 'existenceConfirmed' an authoritative catalogue or database confirms this part number exists, without any document being read; 'seriesConfirmed' the retrieved document covers this part's SERIES but does not print this individual order code; 'partNamed' the retrieved document names this exact part number; 'valuesReadFromSource' the stored VALUES for the fields listed in `fields` were actually read or re-derived from the source — the only value that asserts the NUMBERS were checked, and deliberately the hardest to claim; 'disproven' the source was retrieved and CONTRADICTS this record (does not mention the part, or names a different one); 'inferredNotVerified' the entry was constructed from the record itself (its own URL, its own manufacturer name, a templated search query) with no retrieval of any kind — such an entry is NOT evidence and must never be counted as a citation.

verificationDate.description: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) on which the act recorded in `verification` was performed. Distinct from `retrievedDate`, which dates the DATA; this dates the CHECK. Required whenever `verification` is present and is not 'notAttempted'.

verificationMethod.description: The measurement CONDITIONS and bounds under which the source states the value, read off the source and kept because the schema has nowhere else for them — e.g. 'Measured at 10 mA Max.', '200V AC for 1 minute', 'Dielectric Withstanding Voltage 1000 VRMS Min', 'Ptot max, TC=25 C', 'Qg 55 nC (VGS 10 V)'. Several fields are typed as bare numbers, so the Min/Max sense and the RMS or temperature basis survive only here. This is NOT a place to record HOW the row was obtained: no endpoint or HTTP method, no script or tool name, no staging path, no matcher rule, no ticket number, no agent or campaign identity, no audit note or superseded-value history. That belongs in the commit and the issue tracker — it is not part of the record. It must not be written into `sourceName` either.

derivation.description: For source='derived': the rule the value follows, as a short phrase (e.g. 'contact array from pitch, positions and rows', 'IPC-7351B nominal land pattern for the case code'). No field paths, scripts, tools, ticket numbers or reasoning.

retracted.description: true when this entry has been WITHDRAWN: the claim it records is no longer asserted. A retracted entry is KEPT, never deleted, so the withdrawal stays traceable — but consumers MUST NOT count it as provenance for any field, and MUST NOT treat its sourceUrl/sourceName as a live citation. This exists because a withdrawal has nowhere to live today and is therefore written as a NEW entry that impersonates a source: 91,416 TAS entries carry retraction prose in `sourceName`, spread across five different `source` enum values for the same act.

retractionReason.description: Why the entry was withdrawn, as a short label. Required when `retracted` is true. E.g. 'placeholder value', 'cited document is for a different part', 'superseded'. No history, reasoning or ticket numbers. The fields the withdrawal covers go in `fields`, exactly as for a positive claim.

sourceName.description: Human-readable source identifier, e.g. 'TI parametric API', 'WE - Passive Components.mdb', 'DigiKey'. A NAME ONLY. Verification state belongs in `verification`/`verificationMethod`, a withdrawal in `retracted`/`retractionReason`, and a computation in `derivation` — none of it in this field. Writing them here is what produced 507 distinct bracketed phrasings of what should be a closed vocabulary.

sourceUrl.description: URL the data was retrieved from, if applicable. MUST NOT be set when source='derived': a computation has nothing to retrieve, and a URL on a derived entry reads as a citation that was never made (37,075 such entries exist in the TAS corpus today, 315 of them citing a URL scheme retired in 2026). Put the inputs in `derivation` instead.

retrievedDate.description: Date the data was retrieved (YYYY-MM-DD). For source='derived' there is nothing to retrieve, so this is the date the value was COMPUTED — the two readings are deliberately unified rather than given separate keys, because in both cases the question it answers is 'as of when is this true'.

fields.description: Optional: which fields of this record this source provided (for mixed-source records). On a part that means datasheetInfo fields; on a record with no datasheetInfo (e.g. a CIAS brick) it means whatever fields the source is claiming.

allOf.$comment: PHASE A (additive). A verification claim must say when it was made. Constrains only entries that opt into `verification`; every entry written before this key existed is unaffected.
PHASE A (additive). A withdrawal must say why. Constrains only entries that opt into `retracted: true`.

pinFunction.title: pinFunction
pinFunction.description: Normalized electrical ROLE of one physical terminal — the family-wide controlled vocabulary, hoisted to PEAS (2026-08) from the previously divergent module-local copies (AAS pinout.function 25-value enum, CONAS contactSystem signalRole 7-value enum, CTAS pins.function free string). One vocabulary so a controller's 'ground' and an op-amp's 'ground' are machine-comparable. This is the ROLE axis only: electrical direction is implied by the role (dataIn/dataOut), active level lives in pin.polarity, output topology in family extensions (AAS outputStage), and pad geometry in landPattern. Values are grouped: generic (signal/power/ground/shield/mechanical/noConnect/doNotConnect/other), differential pair halves, analog amplifier roles, supply rails, control, digital data/bus, power-semiconductor terminals, magnetic winding ends, and the power-controller vocabulary merged from CTAS controllerPinFunction (2026-08; normalized on merge: gnd->ground, and the duplicate feedback/compensation/enable/address/noConnect/gate entries deduplicated). 'mechanical' is a terminal with no electrical function (mounting post, board-lock). 'doNotConnect' is a datasheet DNC (internally bonded — must stay open), distinct from 'noConnect' (not bonded).

pin.title: pin
pin.description: One physical terminal of a packaged component: the (pin, name, function) triple that decides drop-in compatibility (same package does NOT imply same pinout — three mutually incompatible SOIC-8 single-op-amp pinouts exist). 'pin' is the designator as printed ('1', 'A2', 'G'); 'name' preserves the datasheet's own label verbatim ('IN+', 'NC/TRIM'); 'function' is the normalized cross-family vocabulary. OPEN MIXIN BASE (like datasheetInfoPartBase): deliberately not sealed here so a family may extend it via the sanctioned allOf idiom (e.g. AAS adds outputStage) — every consumer MUST seal with top-level unevaluatedProperties:false. Direct unextended use: $ref #/$defs/pinout, which is pre-sealed.
Pin number / ball / terminal designator, as printed ('1', 'A2', 'G', 'TAB').

name.description: Datasheet pin name verbatim ('IN+', 'DIS', 'VBUS', 'NC/TRIM').

polarity.description: Active level, for control pins where a swap breaks drop-in compatibility.

pinout.title: pinout
pinout.description: Per-terminal function map — one sealed entry per package pin/ball/terminal. The deciding axis for interchangeability of packaged parts. Families needing extra per-pin fields do NOT re-implement this: they build their own array whose items are allOf [pin, extension] sealed with unevaluatedProperties:false (see AAS). Register maps and per-pin absolute-max ratings are deliberately out of scope — they are not parametric pinout properties.

landPatternPad.title: landPatternPad
landPatternPad.description: One pad or hole of a manufacturer-recommended PCB land pattern. Geometry (shape) is deliberately separate from through-board character (drill/plated) — conflating them (a 'plated-hole' shape) cannot express a rectangular THT pad; KiCad separates pad type from pad shape for the same reason. SMT pad: no drill. THT/press-fit pad: drill (+ copper size). Non-plated mechanical hole: drill + plated:false, no width. Slotted hole (terminal blocks): drill = slot short dimension + slotLength.

id.description: Pad designator as printed in the land-pattern drawing. Joins pinout[].pin (and, for connectors, the CONAS contactSystem contact id) where applicable; purely mechanical pads use their own ids ('MH1').

x.description: Pad-centre X in the land-pattern frame, in m (see landPattern.originDatum).

y.description: Pad-centre Y in the land-pattern frame, in m.

rotation.description: Rotation of the pad about its own centre, in degrees counter-clockwise; 0 (the default when absent) puts width along +X. Degrees are a documented exception to SI radians, matching the MAS coil turn-rotation convention and universal EDA practice.

shape.description: Copper (or hole) outline. Pure geometry — never encodes plating.

width.description: Copper size along the pad's local X (before rotation), in m; the diameter for round pads. Omit for hole-only pads.

height.description: Copper size along the pad's local Y, in m. Omit for round pads.

drill.description: Finished hole diameter, in m; presence marks a through-board pad (THT / press-fit / mechanical). When slotLength is present this is the slot's short dimension.

slotLength.description: Long dimension of a slotted (oval) drill, in m. Requires drill.

plated.description: Whether the hole barrel is plated. Only meaningful together with drill; omit for SMT pads.

landPattern.title: landPattern
landPattern.description: Manufacturer-RECOMMENDED PCB land pattern (the 'recommended layout' drawing of the datasheet): pad centres, copper sizes and drills, exactly as published. Datasheet-layer facts only — no derived values, no courtyard/keep-out/3-D envelope (those stay family-side, e.g. CONAS geometry.keepOut/boundingEnvelope). Distinct from any scalar mounting-area figure (CAS capacitor 'footprint' is an area in m^2 and is NOT this type). Family-wide shared type hoisted to PEAS (2026-08); previously only CONAS carried a local variant.

pattern.description: Coarse topology hint for browse/filter; the pads array is the authority.

originDatum.description: What (0,0) of the pad coordinates refers to. A coordinate list with no stated datum is not reusable data.

recommendedBoardThickness.description: Board thickness the pattern is specified for, in m, when the datasheet states one (press-fit patterns are thickness-specific).

pads.description: Land/hole pattern, one entry per pad.

sParameterReference.title: sParameterReference
sParameterReference.description: Reference to a MEASURED (or vendor-solver) S-parameter file published by its rights holder — a POINTER, never the payload. Policy (approved 2026-08, ABT #470): we reference vendor Touchstone, we never host it (single-vendor click-through licences) and we never synthesize it (a synthetic .s4p is indistinguishable from a measurement and would be rightly rejected). The checksum lets a consumer detect silent upstream replacement; retrievedDate records when the URI last resolved (a cited URL counts only once fetched).

uri.description: Where the rights holder publishes the file (or the request page when download is form-gated).

ports.description: Port count of the referenced file (e.g. 4 for a .s4p).

source.description: Who published it and what it is (e.g. 'Samtec High Speed Characterization, SEAM-40 + SEAF-40 mated pair').

licenceNote.description: Access/licence condition observed at retrievedDate (e.g. 'free download, no login', 'request form, 24 h turnaround').

checksum.description: sha256 of the file as fetched at retrievedDate, hex — drift detection only, never redistribution.

retrievedDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD the URI was last verified to resolve.

schemaVersion.title: Schema version
schemaVersion.description: The release of the schema package that defines the document carrying this value, as a Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 string: a MAS document carries the MAS release it conforms to, a CAS document the CAS release, and so on. Every module's top-level document may carry it under the property name schemaVersion. Optional; if absent, the latest release of the document's package is assumed. Because of that, a tool that migrates a document written against an older release must stamp the release it migrated to, or the document will be read as the latest. A consumer that does not support the MAJOR version of a present value must reject the document rather than guess.
schemaVersion.$comment: Pattern is the official SemVer 2.0.0 regular expression, numbered-capture-group variant, copied unchanged from https://semver.org/#is-there-a-suggested-regular-expression-regex-to-check-a-semver-string
